title: Prove one useful OpenCV 5.1 CUDA chain on the RTX 4090 and freeze its build

probe_scope.mode: read-only inspection plus a B1 compile/run probe
performed: machine and toolchain probes: nvidia-smi, nvcc, cmake, py -0p, python, MSVC/vswhere, cl version banner, Windows SDK, CUDA arch lists, cuDNN search, disk, cpu/ram
installed-cv2 inspection: version, resolved path, installed distributions, cuda device count, presence of the cudaarithm masked meanStdDev overload
independent source-pin verification with git ls-remote (refs only, no clone)
read of blueprint sections 8.1, 8.2, 10 and 11, and of RULING-2026-11-06

round two (2026-11-07): B1 compile/run probe — sourced vcvars64, compiled .scratch/gpu_probe/vectorAdd.cu with nvcc 13.3 -arch=sm_89 (exit 0), and ran vectorAdd.exe on the RTX 4090 (exit 0, 0 mismatches); see round_two_probe
round two (2026-11-07): wrote the probe source, batch file and binary to .scratch/gpu_probe/ (gitignored at every depth)
not_performed: no git clone of opencv or opencv_contrib
round one only: no compiler invocation on any .cu or .cpp source file (SUPERSEDED in round two — see round_two_probe)
round one only: no build, no install, no pip install, no venv creation
round one only: no file write outside this receipt (round two wrote .scratch/gpu_probe/, which is gitignored)
probe_scope.network_touched: github.com via git ls-remote (read-only, refs only, no clone)

verdict.one_line: B1 is closed: nvcc 13.3 compiles with MSVC 19.44 and the resulting sm_89 binary runs on the RTX 4090. Every other input the route needs is present (CUDA 13.3, CMake 4.2.1, 48 cores, 1.13 TiB free), but no OpenCV source build exists, so no CUDA chain is proven.
proven_by_observation: the target GPU is an RTX 4090 (sm_89) and nvcc 13.3 lists compute_89 and sm_89
CUDA toolkit 13.3 (V13.3.73) is installed and is first on PATH; CUDA_PATH points at v13.3
a VS 2022 BuildTools toolset (14.44.35207, cl 19.44.35222, x64, Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0) is installed; cl is not on PATH until vcvars64 is sourced
CMake 4.2.1 is installed and resolves first to C:/Python314/Scripts/cmake.exe
the machine has 48 logical processors, 127.5 GiB RAM, and 1131.1 GiB free on C:
the installed OpenCV is a CPU-only wheel: cv2.cuda.getCudaEnabledDeviceCount() is 0 and cv2.cuda.meanStdDev does not exist on it
the pinned upstream tag 5.1.0 in both repositories peels to the blueprint's exact commits (verified by git ls-remote)
there are no OpenCV sources, no build cache and no worker venv on this box

nvcc 13.3 (V13.3.73) accepts MSVC 19.44.35222 / toolset 14.44.35207 as its host compiler: vectorAdd.cu compiled with -arch=sm_89 (exit 0) and the binary ran on the RTX 4090 (exit 0, 0 mismatches) — see round_two_probe
not_proven: that CMake 4.2.1 configures OpenCV 5.1 plus its vendored dependencies
that BUILD_LIST=core,cudaarithm,python3 generates the python3 bindings and the CUDA arithmetic module
that a Python binding for the chosen interpreter builds at all
that the masked Python cv2.cuda.meanStdDev overload exists, or its output shape, precision, mask type, empty/singleton behaviour and population convention
that the named useful chain (split + addWeighted -> masked meanStdDev -> compare/mask/countNonZero -> sync) executes on the GPU
build duration, artifact size, and final native-file digests

sources_pinned.note: the blueprint and both live tags agree exactly; no source revision is guessed

build_route.route: native CMake source build of OpenCV 5.1 plus matching opencv_contrib with CUDA; never the opencv-python wheel
build_route.decided_by: RULING-2026-11-06 D6 (source-built OpenCV 5.1 + opencv_contrib with CUDA)
build_route.why_not_the_wheel: the installed wheel is CPU-only: cv2.cuda.getCudaEnabledDeviceCount() is 0 and cv2.cuda.meanStdDev is absent; published opencv-python wheels remain a CPU-only route (blueprint:188)
build_route.build_root_reason: short path keeps the tree under the Windows 260-character limit; clone, build and install stay siblings

interpreter_abi.owner: WP1 output, per RULING-2026-11-06 D1 caveat (ABI is recorded from the probe, never guessed)

candidates.note: the only 3.13 on this box is the Microsoft Store alias, which is not itself a build substrate; a python.org or uv CPython 3.13 must be provisioned before configure if 3.13 is picked

recorded_not_in_candidate_set.note: host default recorded in round one; not part of the round-two candidate set

interpreter_abi.forbidden: hython 3.13 (blueprint:61); the Microsoft Store 3.13 alias is not a build substrate (a provisioned CPython 3.13 is)
interpreter_abi.consequence: the Python binding is interpreter-ABI-specific; the venv must exist before configure and PYTHON3_EXECUTABLE must be pinned to it, or the generated module will not import
interpreter_abi.recommendation: decide before any build work; the choice is a product decision, not something this probe can settle

flags.parallelism: /m:32 chosen to leave headroom; 48 logical cores are available, so /m:48 is possible only when the box is otherwise idle (RULING operating rule 1: development in tandem, never displacing a running task)
flags.fallback_1: add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 if CMake 4.2.1 rejects a vendored dependency's cmake_minimum_required(<3.5)
flags.fallback_2: drop BUILD_LIST and build the default module set with CUDA ON if BUILD_LIST does not generate both python3 and cudaarithm

rationale.cuda_arch_bin_89: sm_89 is the RTX 4090; nvcc 13.3 lists compute_89 and sm_89, so it is buildable. Building all 12 listed architectures would cost hours for no benefit
rationale.cudaarithm: it lives in opencv_contrib and supplies the arithmetic the blueprint's chain names (addWeighted, meanStdDev, compare, countNonZero)
rationale.with_cudnn_off: no cuDNN exists on this box, and blueprint:278 excludes DNN/cuDNN from the first classical-QC slice
rationale.build_list_trim: core + cudaarithm + python3 is the smallest module set that can answer the question; a full default build is the fallback only

cost.reason: no configure, compile or install was performed in this probe; no duration is quoted from core count

hard_rules: never install the built cv2 into Houdini's Python
never install into C:/Users/User/AppData/Roaming/Python/Python314/site-packages (the CPU wheel already lives there)
keep worker cv2/OIIO/CUDA binaries outside Houdini's Python and DLL search path (blueprint:238)
the zero-host-cv2 lint tests/test_retina_boundary.py:67 must stay green

blockers.statement: MSVC 19.44.35222 / toolset 14.44 (VS 17.14) against CUDA 13.3 is unverified. nvcc's host_config.h may reject _MSC_VER 1944.
blockers.evidence: round one: cl reports 19.44.35222 for x64; toolset dir is 14.44.35207; nvcc is V13.3.73. ROUND TWO (2026-11-07): sourced vcvars64, compiled .scratch/gpu_probe/vectorAdd.cu with nvcc 13.3 -arch=sm_89 — exit 0, vectorAdd.exe produced (172544 bytes); the exe ran on the RTX 4090 (cc 8.9) with exit 0 and 0 mismatches. nvcc does NOT reject _MSC_VER 1944.
blockers.resolution: resolved by observation on 2026-11-07; no toolset pin and no CUDA downgrade is needed for B1. Evidence: round_two_probe.

blockers.statement: The worker Python ABI is not chosen. The binding is ABI-specific and retina/.venv does not exist.
blockers.evidence: ROUND TWO candidate set recorded, NOT chosen: CPython 3.12 (3.12.10, real install) and CPython 3.13 (only a Microsoft Store alias exists on this box; a provisioned 3.13 would be required). 3.14.2 was recorded in round one but is not a round-two candidate. retina/.venv is absent; RULING D1 caveat makes the ABI a WP1 output; blueprint:61 forbids hython. See build_route.interpreter_abi.
blockers.resolution: owner/WP1 picks between CPython 3.12 and CPython 3.13; then create the venv and pin PYTHON3_EXECUTABLE before configure.

blockers.statement: There are no OpenCV sources, no build cache and no worker venv on this box.
blockers.evidence: C:/ocv does not exist; no *opencv* directory under the worktree; retina/.venv absent.
blockers.resolution: two shallow clones (about 1-2 GB) then configure; disk is not a constraint (1131.1 GiB free) and GitHub is reachable (ls-remote succeeded).

blockers.statement: CMake 4.2.1 removed compatibility with cmake_minimum_required(VERSION <3.5), which vendored third-party dependencies can trip.
blockers.evidence: cmake --version is 4.2.1; OpenCV 5.1's vendored deps were not configured.
blockers.resolution: -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5, or pin CMake 3.31 in the build venv.

blockers.statement: BUILD_LIST=core,cudaarithm,python3 may not generate the Python bindings as expected; OpenCV's BUILD_LIST / BUILD_opencv_python3 interaction is a known configure-time trap.
blockers.evidence: not configured; the interaction was not probed.
blockers.resolution: inspect the configure summary for the python3 module; on failure drop BUILD_LIST and build the default module set with CUDA ON.

blockers.statement: Source support is not binding support. The blueprint requires a Python masked cv2.cuda.meanStdDev with a CV_8UC1 mask, its output shape and precision, empty/singleton behaviour and population convention.
blockers.evidence: the installed CPU wheel has a cv2.cuda module but no cv2.cuda.meanStdDev attribute at all, so the overload's Python shape cannot be read off the wheel; C++ source support does not establish a working binding (blueprint:217).
blockers.resolution: after the build, execute the masked probe on the 11x11 fixture and record the actual signature, dtype and semantics; qualification is NR-GPU-QUALIFICATION's job.

blockers.statement: Global site-packages pollution: cv2 4.12.0 already resolves from the user site, and two OpenCV distributions are installed there.
blockers.evidence: cv2 resolves to C:/Users/User/AppData/Roaming/Python/Python314/site-packages/cv2; distributions are opencv-python and opencv-python-headless; the zero-cv2 host lint is tests/test_retina_boundary.py:67.
blockers.resolution: build and install only inside the isolated worker venv; never pip install there into global site-packages.

blockers.statement: Windows path length: OpenCV build trees can exceed 260 characters.
blockers.evidence: repository depth plus a build tree under a nested path would be long.
blockers.resolution: use the short root C:/ocv with clone, build and install as siblings.

blockers.statement: Build time and artifact size are unmeasured.
blockers.evidence: no configure or compile was run. graph.json rates the node effort L.
blockers.resolution: time the configure and the compile; do not convert 48 cores into an estimate.

blockers.statement: The minimum driver for a CUDA 13.3 runtime was not independently verified.
blockers.evidence: driver 621.14 reports CUDA UMD 13.5, which is newer than the 13.3 toolkit build, so the direction is favourable but not proven by a vendor table.
blockers.resolution: record the driver range actually tested in the build receipt.

blockers.evidence: recursive cudnn* search under CUDA/v13.3 returns nothing.
blockers.resolution: WITH_CUDNN=OFF; no cuda-dnn module. The named classical chain does not need it and blueprint:278 excludes it from the first slice.

closure.proposed_real_closure: the chosen worker venv's python imports cv2, cv2.__file__ resolves inside that venv, cv2.cuda.getCudaEnabledDeviceCount() equals 1, and cv2.cuda.meanStdDev(src, mask) executes and returns the masked mean/std for the 11x11 fixture, matches an independent CPU reference within a frozen FP32 tolerance, and the receipt records the executed dispatch branch plus artifact digests
